chapter: Learning piano, dancing and Alphonso Trent
title: Learning from Trent and his first paid piano job in Athens, Texas
summary: Trent lets him sit in on rehearsals and teaches him; he gets his first professional job in Athens, and is thrown out of a club after playing only one song.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, Alphonso was the piano player. He liked me and he used to...then I used to start bugging him to show me things. Whenever we would go...say if we were playing the Adolphus Hotel, we may arrive at the place an hour before, you understand, and he may be practicing like, learning a new song or something. I could sit in on the rehearsals. I began to hear, you know, "That's a B-flat...tune your horn," and that business. So I had an opportunity to learn something about music and about the piano and about how to play soft, and tonal quality and, you know, various rhythms and that thing. That really started me then...... you couldn't stop me. Then I got a job...a man heard...by this time there was some talk that, "Sam Price is dancing with the Alphonso Trent Band," and,

"Sam Price has learned...man, he's playing the piano," and this, that and the other. You know, I could play the Charleston, you know I could play 'My Isle of Golden Dreams' the "Charleston," or whatever there it was, I'd play these things. So finally this man came to me and said, he wanted me to come to Athens, Texas, to play for a dance. He'd pay me five dollars a night for a Saturday and Sunday. And I could...Christmas was on Monday, so I had an opportunity to go and play for him and come back and be home in time for Christmas. So that was the first professional job I said that I had. Just the piano...it was out of tune...and you know what I mean. But before that I had so much nerve that a guy came looking for a piano player to play for a man that wanted somebody to play for him, so I said, 'I play the piano, so the guy took me up to this club, big club, and this guy was sitting there with a bottle of whiskey and he said, "play me some music!"' And I played 'My Isle of Golden Dreams$ ." Then he said, 'okay, now, play me some blues. I played 'My Isle of Golden Dream$' He says, "Okay, play me something with the Charleston. I played, 'My Isle .." He told me, "Get the hell out of here," and he gave me five dollars. That was the first...(laughter). So now we are up to that first job.
